decisions.reason: As a low-visibility extension of the core radiant-heater business, it remains easier to cut than the flagship lines, but another year of continued offering, modest sunk costs, and the firm's growth still favor retention.
This multi-model electric flagship is closely tied to the firm's publicly stated lower-carbon direction, so accumulated investment and the need to justify that strategy make withdrawal unlikely.

Although not central to the announced strategic shift and therefore the most exposed of the remaining visible products, its survival so far, portfolio fit, and the firm's expansion still make continued support more likely than exit.

The hydrogen-capable line is highly visible, explicitly connected to the firm's future orientation, and already publicly validated by a named real-world launch, so escalation of commitment strongly supports keeping it.
